compiler_spec.usage: Locked BfdArchitecture initializes the oracle Funcdata; the Rust projection retains the same architecture/compiler identity and an equivalent raw stderr message sink.

analysis_options.action_entry: Direct ActionPool::apply on one enabled live PcodeOp; warnings and breakpoints disabled; OPACTION_DEBUG absent.
analysis_options.op_iteration: One pre-existing live op only; no op insertion, deletion, or dynamic-tree boundary is exercised.
analysis_options.rules: Four scripted rules in insertion order: change and old_tail register for SUBPIECE; new_head and new_tail register for INT_ZEXT. change removes slot 1, changes opcode to INT_ZEXT, and returns the case value.
analysis_options.architecture_state: Locked oracle owns a fully initialized BfdArchitecture/ScopeLocal for pinned GetStr. Rust owns Architecture::new with identical archid and raw stderr print contract but lacks the remaining BFD/type/symbol state. ActionPool does not read those absent fields in the covered projection; the complete same-input claim remains unavailable and overall status is MISMATCH.
analysis_options.diagnostics: The oracle BfdArchitecture uses an isolated ostringstream. Initialization/loader diagnostics are discarded before each target case; each case's ActionPool-produced bytes are forwarded unmodified to process stderr. Rust forwards Architecture::print_message unmodified. No runner filtering or prefix normalization is performed.
analysis_options.initialization: Both sides construct a block at ram:0x1000 and one alive SUBPIECE with unique:4 output, register:0x20:2 input 0, constant:0:4 input 1, identical creation time/order, and no other ops. The C++ direct-apply probe initializes inherited count/lcount to zero because Action::perform is intentionally bypassed.
analysis_options.counters: Locked Rule::count_tests/count_apply are observed directly. Rust Rule has no framework counters, so fixture-local counters record identical attempted/successful scripted calls; this is an explicit residual, not a complete Rule-state match.
analysis_options.normalization: None; stdout fields, raw stderr bytes, rule/event order, and target op state are preserved.

binary.source_policy: Materialize the pinned provenance commit's examples/curl Git blob by verified object ID; never read the working-tree file and never require runtime HEAD equality

cases.expected_raw_diagnostic: ERROR: Rule change changed op without returning result of 1!

matched_projection: After change, old_tail is abandoned and the INT_ZEXT rule list restarts at new_head/index 0 in both return-value cases.
The zero-result opcode change emits the locked diagnostic byte-for-byte through the Architecture sink.
Final opcode/eval flags/input/output shape and storage, lifecycle, parent/address/time/order, bank membership, and removed-input descendant state match.
Enabled scripted rule attempt/success observations match in fixed insertion order.
known_differences: Ghidra ActionPool::apply returns 0 and stores positive change in inherited Action::count; Rugra apply returns the positive change and its private total is not exposed.
Rugra Rule lacks disabled state and framework count_tests/count_apply; fixture-local counters only prove enabled rule invocation in this projection.
Rugra Rule/ActionPool lacks issueWarning, rule action breakpoints, and resumable op_state/rule_index.
Ghidra dynamically traverses PcodeOpTree and calls opDeadAndGone for an initially dead op; Rugra snapshots alivelist into Vec and skips dead entries without destruction.
Rust fixture Architecture is not the complete BfdArchitecture/type/symbol state; only the identity and consumed print-message contract are equivalent.
